miracles.title: Mary Appears Over a Cairo Church — Zeitoun, Egypt (April 2, 1968 – 1971)
miracles.description:
For almost three years, people in Cairo saw a glowing figure above a church. Many said it looked like Mary. It happened at night, several times a week.

The first people to see it were two Muslim workers across the street. They thought a woman was about to fall off the roof, so they shouted up to warn her.

After that, huge crowds came. Muslims, Christians, Jews, and people with no religion all watched together. Egypt's government sent investigators to check for tricks — lights, projectors, mirrors. They found nothing. Many Muslims in the crowd called her 'Maryam,' the name she already holds in Islam.
miracles.testimony_highlight: First reported by Muslim transit-authority workers on watch across from the church, not by churchgoers.
miracles.documentation_level: Strong — covered by Egyptian press and international outlets, investigated by government authorities and church officials of multiple denominations.
prompts: Search: 'Zeitoun Nasser government investigation Marian apparition'

miracles.title: Mary and the Miracle of the Sun — Fátima, Portugal (October 13, 1917)
miracles.description:
Three shepherd children said Mary promised a sign, so that everyone would have a reason to believe them. Up to 100,000 people came to see it, in muddy fields. Some were reporters sent to prove it was a hoax.

People said the sun began to spin and change color, like it was dancing in the sky. The wet ground and people's soaked clothes dried in just a few minutes.

Many newspapers wrote about it that day — even ones that did not support the Church. That is a big reason people still trust this story today.
miracles.testimony_highlight: Reported by secular and anti-Catholic Portuguese newspapers, not only religious ones.
miracles.documentation_level: Strong — extensive contemporary press coverage across the political spectrum; later reviewed in a canonical Church investigation.
prompts: Search YouTube: 'Fatima 1917 Miracle of the Sun witnesses'
Search: 'Fatima Miracle of the Sun newspaper archive 1917'

miracles.title: Mary Protects a Village During the Boxer Rebellion — Donglü, China (April 1900)
miracles.description:
In 1900, soldiers attacked a small Christian village in China. This happened during a time when Christians across the country were being killed.

Villagers say a woman in white, glowing with light, appeared in the sky above their church. The soldiers fired at her, but she did not disappear.

Soon after, the soldiers fled in fear. Some say a rider on a horse chased them away. The village survived that year — almost none of the others nearby did. People still honor this story today as Our Lady of China.
miracles.testimony_highlight: Attackers themselves are said to have described what frightened them off, not only the villagers being defended.
miracles.documentation_level: Moderate — rests on community and missionary testimony passed down from the period rather than independent contemporary press investigation; treat as strong oral history, not forensic proof.

miracles.title: Mary Hidden in Plain Sight — Kakure Kirishitan, Japan (1614–1873)
miracles.description:
Long ago, Japan made it illegal to be Christian. People could be killed just for practicing the faith.

Even so, some families kept it secret for over 200 years. They carved statues of Mary to look like Kannon, a Buddhist figure of mercy. This way, no one outside the family could tell what the statue really meant.

Behind closed doors, they prayed to these hidden statues as Mary, for about ten generations. Many of these 'Maria Kannon' statues still exist today, in museums and old family homes.
miracles.testimony_highlight: An entire underground society, not individual visionaries, sustained her image for over two centuries.
miracles.documentation_level: Strong as documented social and religious history — surviving Maria Kannon statues, village records, and missionary accounts confirm the practice, though it is a pattern of devotion rather than a single witnessed event.
prompts: Search YouTube: 'Hidden Christians Japan Maria Kannon documentary'
Search: 'Maria Kannon statue hidden Christians Japan museum'

miracles.title: Comfort in the Jungle — La Vang, Vietnam (c. 1798)
miracles.description:
In Vietnam, a ruler was trying to wipe out Christianity. Families ran into the jungle to hide and stay alive.

A whole group sheltering there — not just one person — said a woman appeared to comfort them. She told them to boil leaves from a nearby tree to make medicine. That plant remedy is real, and people still use it in the area today.

La Vang is now Vietnam's most visited place connected to Mary. Buddhist and non-religious visitors go there too, not just Christians.
miracles.testimony_highlight: Reported by a whole group of persecuted families sheltering together, and tied to a real, still-used herbal remedy.
miracles.documentation_level: Moderate — rests on community testimony carried through persecuted congregations rather than outside investigation; the plant remedy's continued regional use is independently verifiable.
prompts: Search YouTube: 'La Vang shrine Vietnam history'

miracles.title: A Weeping Statue — Our Lady of Akita, Japan (1973–1981)
miracles.description:
In a small convent in Japan, a wooden statue of Mary began to cry. This happened more than 100 times over several years, and other people saw it too — not just the nun who found it first.

At first it looked like tears. Later, the liquid looked like blood. Scientists at a university lab tested it. They were not Catholic and had no reason to make the story bigger than it was.

The tests showed the liquid was real, from a human body. No one could explain how it got on a wooden statue. The story is still talked about across Japan today.
miracles.testimony_highlight: Fluid samples were independently analyzed by university forensic scientists who were not part of the Catholic Church.
miracles.documentation_level: Strong for the physical evidence — the forensic analysis is documented; the interpretation of its cause remains a matter of belief.
prompts: Search YouTube: 'Akita weeping statue Japan investigation'
Search: 'Akita statue tears forensic analysis university'

miracles.title: A Light Over Giza — Our Lady of Warraq, Egypt (December 2009)
miracles.description:
In 2009, near Cairo, a Muslim man sitting at a coffee shop noticed something strange. He saw a bright light coming from a nearby church and pointed it out to the people around him.

He was the first person to see it. Over the next few nights, more people came — Muslims and Christians together — to watch the light over the church roof.

This story looks a lot like what happened at Zeitoun, decades earlier. It shows the same pattern: someone from outside the faith sees it first.
miracles.testimony_highlight: First witness was reportedly a Muslim bystander at a coffee shop, echoing the Zeitoun pattern four decades later.
miracles.documentation_level: Moderate — reported in regional press at the time; less independently investigated than Zeitoun or Fátima.
prompts: Search: 'Our Lady of Warraq Giza 2009 apparition'
